author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This solution pads the string with `'1'` sentinels on both ends, then does a **run-length encoding** pass, building a `stack` of `[character, runLength]` pairs while counting the total number of `1`s (`ones`). It then scans the internal `1`-runs and, for each isolated `'1'` sitting between two zero-runs, checks whether **flipping that single `1`** would merge the adjacent zero-runs, tracking the largest combined run found. The final answer is `ones - 2` (to remove the two sentinel `1`s) plus that best possible merge.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This attempt builds `prefixSum` and `suffixSum` arrays tracking the length of the **contiguous run of `0`s** ending at (or starting from) each index, alongside a running count of `1`s. It then looks for the position with the largest `prefixSum[i] + suffixSum[i]` where both are positive, treating that as the best pair of zero-runs a single flipped `1` could join, and returns `ones + maxZeros`. It **fails** because it never handles the edge case where the string has no `1`s at all, letting `maxZeros` and `ones` combine into a wrong result.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This is the same **prefix/suffix zero-run** technique as before, now adding an early `return 0` when the string contains no `1`s at all. It still **fails**, though, because when scanning for the best `prefixSum[i] + suffixSum[i]` pair it never verifies that position `i` is actually a `1` character, so it can wrongly merge two zero-runs that aren't separated by a flippable `1`.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This corrected version refines the **prefix/suffix zero-run** technique by 1-indexing the `prefixSum`/`suffixSum` arrays and, crucially, checking `s[i - 1] === '1'` before combining them, so a merge is only counted when it's genuinely centered on a `1` character between two zero-runs. It returns `0` immediately if the string has no `1`s, otherwise it returns the total `ones` count plus the best combined zero-run length found this way.
